root_cause.text: In f2fs foreground garbage collection (FGGC), node block migration does not clear the fsync and dentry marks on node pages before writing them to disk, unlike background GC which clears them via f2fs_sync_node_pages(), causing fsck to misinterpret migrated blocks as user-issued fsync writes.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the set/clear of fsync and dentry marks into __write_node_folio and ensures that when called from the FGGC path (f2fs_write_single_node_folio), it passes `do_fsync=false` and calls `set_dentry_mark(folio, false)`, thus clearing the marks. The commit description explicitly states: "The root cause is that GC does not clear the dentry mark and fsync mark during node block migration" and "In BGGC mode, node block migration is handled by f2fs_sync_node_pages(), which guarantees the dentry and fsync marks are cleared before writing."

candidates.rationale: The call to __write_node_folio in the foreground GC path does not clear fsync/dentry marks before writing, leaving stale marks that mislead fsck.
The GC IO type is specified, and no clearing of fsync/dentry marks occurs prior to this write, directly causing the vulnerability.
This condition in __write_node_folio may incorrectly set dentry marks because the fsync mark was not cleared before the GC write, causing is_fsync_dnode to return a stale value.
The set_dentry_mark call is made without ensuring previous marks were cleared, so in the GC path it can set a dentry mark that should not be present, contributing to fsck misinterpretation.
The argument to set_dentry_mark may evaluate to true due to uncleared fsync marks, causing an incorrect dentry mark to be persisted during GC.
